name: Reasoning Compression via Step-Entropy Analysis
executive_summary: Compress long chain-of-thought reasoning by identifying and removing low-information-content steps, cutting latency without proportionally hurting accuracy.
description: Analyzes the entropy contributed by each step of an already-generated CoT trace and prunes or condenses low-entropy (low-information) steps, on the premise that not every reasoning step contributes equally to the final answer. Positioned as an efficiency layer on top of existing reasoning-elicitation techniques rather than a new elicitation method in its own right.
when_to_use: Base CoT/reasoning traces are verbose and latency/cost is a binding constraint.
when_not_to_use: Reasoning traces are already short, or interpretability of the full trace matters more than compression.
known_pitfalls: Aggressive compression risks removing a step that looked low-information locally but was load-bearing for correctness.

primary_source.title: Making Slow Thinking Faster: Step-Entropy Guided Reasoning Compression

usage_templates.template:
Here is a chain-of-thought reasoning trace: {{full_reasoning_trace}}

Identify which steps are load-bearing for the final answer and which are low-information restatements or filler. Rewrite the trace keeping only the load-bearing steps, preserving the final answer exactly.
usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
